newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jakarta, Bangkok indices poised to cross paths.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta, Bangkok indices poised to cross paths.

text.p: Market indices for Jakarta and Bangkok were about to cross paths on Thursday as Indonesian stocks soared past 700 points while Thai issues looked set to plunge past the same key level.
Jakarta's main stock index gained 6.78 points on Wednesday, taking it above the 700-point mark for the first time to close at 701.06. It was 2.39 points higher at midday on Thursday at 703.44.

However, Thailand's market continued moving in the opposite direction, sliding 17.80 points early on Thursday to 704.77 after closing 11.42 points weaker at 722.57 on Wednesday. A break of the 700 level is now widely expected.
Regional traders said selling in Thailand has persisted for months, and the recent weakness is nothing new. Funds are still overweight on Thailand, suggesting a slump to 650 is likely.
"It may well be cheap now, it may well be overdone, but people are still hanging on to the baby," one trader said. "The problem is, on the way down people couldn't get out."
Concern is mounting that Thailand will start to experience a slew of bank and finance company mergers to avoid failures on bad debt accumulated from a property sector turned sour.
"It won't be so much failure as merger," said Jake van der Kamp, regional strategist with HG Asia in Hong Kong.

"We'll see finance companies merging with banks, takeovers. Thailand is not likely to see outright collapse. The system will come together at some point and they'll simply say, 'We're all in it together -- you take that one, I'll take this one'."
While the Thai market shudders on rumoured merger or bail-out candidates, Jakarta is rolling along on stellar earnings growth and a strong economic performance.

With the market now trading at about 15.5 times 1997 earnings, most forecasts of 20-percent earnings growth through 1998 have prompted expectations of market improvements to at least 18 times earnings, which would take the index to 820-850 points.

"The economy is looking really decent," said van der Kamp. "There are good reasons to expect currency strength, inflation and interest rates are coming down, the government's balancing its books and trade is up while the rest of Asia collapsed."

Jakarta quickly fended off nervousness associated with riots last year. After trading sideways from July until September, Indonesian stocks took off just as the government listed 1.1 billion shares in state-controlled PT Bank Negara Indonesia in November at a price of 850 rupiah.
The shares closed at 1,250 rupiah on the first day of trade and continued to rise. It added 20 rupiah on Thursday to 1,720 rupiah.
Market players said that one issue could not move the entire market despite foreign investment restrictions that occasionally distort trading.
"You wouldn't have found people in for it quite so strongly as they were unless they were generally optimistic about Indonesia," said van der Kamp.

Dealers said fresh money, much of it from Europe, is driving Jakarta shares at the moment. Wednesday's sudden strength was attributed to pent-up demand following a long Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem holiday. Tight liquidity also played a role.
"Yesterday was the first day it was open for a week. It was foreigners -- many locals are still on holiday," one trader said.
A move into second liners is now anticipated.
"What we're seeing is people wanting to weight up in the last two weeks. The run into blue chips might slow down and we'll see some action in second-liners," he said.
